argument.text: Choose a compact time interval J containing t in its interior and a compact C supplied by H003. Outside C, u is locally the constant q, so its first derivatives vanish. Thus e(·,t) is continuous and zero outside C, hence compactly supported. On Euclidean space with Lebesgue measure, opens are measurable and the measure is finite on compact sets; ℝ is a normed additive commutative group. M001 gives integrability of e(·,t). Since t was arbitrary this holds for all t>0.

hypothesis_checks: ℝⁿ has its Borel measurable topology.
Euclidean open sets are Borel measurable.
ℝ is a normed additive commutative group.
Lebesgue measure is finite on compact sets.
e(·,t) is continuous and compactly supported by smoothness and H003.
